units.translation: It is natural to take the ⟦1⟧ as synonymous with ⟦2⟧; see on 624; however, at 1015f. ⟦3⟧ stands unambiguously, and the double accusative is also possible with this ⟦4⟧.
both divinities and mortals inhabiting the city of Pallas

At line 921 ⟦1⟧ as at ⟦2⟧. 139, with no other sense of the ⟦3⟧ than that of intensification; ⟦4⟧ (⟦5⟧. 1213) 'prophesying'; the aorist does not contradict the ⟦6⟧, since this too, transposed into the past, would yield ⟦7⟧ (cf. ⟦8⟧ 928f.). In general, in what follows the form of the wish prevails, not that of prophecy; though when mighty divinities wish, there is hardly a difference between 'may' and 'shall' or 'will'; see what Athena says at 949ff. ⟦9⟧ ⟦10⟧. 1150; I see no reason to correct to the synonymous and only weaker ⟦11⟧ (907), where even of flowing things ⟦12⟧ ⟦13⟧ stands. Bright sunshine (906) will make all other good things sprout from the earth in richest abundance, like the fruits; for the gods and spirits of the deep send all fortune and again all misfortune (⟦14⟧, ⟦15⟧ etc.). ⟦16⟧ seems correctly emended except for the tense; at least from later authors such as Himerius and the Anacreontea Lobeck on Ajax p. 77 brings enough evidence for factitive ⟦17⟧. But the aorist I cannot understand; better the future, connected to ⟦18⟧.

Between the five anapestic passages of Athena there is, as G. Hermann recognized, a responsion, though not corresponding to that of the strophes and antistrophes by which they are separated. Rather, this first passage responds with the last, 1003-1013, but the three middle ones with each other. In a and e a sentence begins in each case with three dimeters; the second, belonging to the same system, can be written as dimeter monom. dim. monom. paroem., if in a after ⟦1⟧ one supplies the missing verb. There follows now a second system in dim. dim. monom. paroemiac.
